//: Import map for the MCP edge function. HAND-WRITTEN — keep it that way.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
`index.ts` beside it is generated by @lovable.dev/mcp-js's Vite plugin and
emits `npm:` specifiers, which is hardcoded (stacks/supabase/vite.js) with no
option to change it. Those specifiers made the function undeployable:
Deploying Function: mcp (script size: 25 MB)
unexpected update function status 413: {"message":"request entity too large"}
`npm:@lovable.dev/mcp-js` resolves to 159 npm packages, because the package is
both a runtime library AND a Vite plugin: it declares esbuild as a runtime
dependency, which drags in every @esbuild/* platform binary (aix-ppc64,
android-arm, darwin-*, freebsd-*, linux-*, win32-*), plus vite, @rolldown and
lightningcss. None of it is reachable from the runtime entry — esbuild is
referenced only by the plugin's own vite.js — but Deno installs a package's
declared tree regardless of what is imported. Measured with `deno info`:
159 npm packages resolved; esbuild 9.5MB + SDK 8.6MB + zod 5.2MB alone is 24MB.
Remapping the same specifiers to esm.sh (which serves tree-shaken, pre-built
ESM instead of whole tarballs) takes the runtime graph to 22 modules / 0.58 MB
— npmPackages: 0. That is ~42x smaller and well under the upload limit.
esm.sh is already this repo's dominant convention for edge functions (366
imports against 66 `npm:` ones), so this is the house style, not a new
dependency.
WHY THE URLS LOOK LIKE THIS — every parameter is load-bearing
target=denonext   Build for the Deno runtime the edge functions run on.
deps=zod@3.25.76  Pin the SDK's transitive zod. @modelcontextprotocol/sdk
accepts `^3.25 || ^4.0`, and esm.sh otherwise resolves it
to zod 4 while our tool schemas are zod 3 — two zod majors
in one bundle. That is not cosmetic: `deno check` fails
(`Property '_zod' is missing in type 'ZodString'`) and at
runtime the SDK would receive schema objects it cannot
recognise. Pinned, the graph contains exactly one zod, the
same 3.25.76 module our own import resolves to, so schema
identity holds.
bundle=all        Required, and not merely an optimisation. With `deps=`
alone esm.sh emits a build-id path whose chunks 404:
/@lovable.dev/mcp-js@0.26.2/X-ZHpvZEAzLjI1Ljc2/denonext/
dist/cors-DnU41czH.mjs -> 404. That failure is invisible to
`deno check` (types resolve from .d.ts, not the .mjs
chunks) and only appears when the module is actually loaded.
`bundle=all` inlines the chunks, so there are none to miss.
VERIFIED, not assumed. Against this exact map, under Deno 2.9.5:
`deno check` clean; the server boots; `initialize` negotiates; `tools/list`
emits the correct JSON Schema derived from the zod schema; `tools/call echo`
returns its input; and an empty string is rejected with the zod `too_small`
error — i.e. the schema round-trips in both directions.
RULES
- Do NOT add a `_lovableMcpGenerated` key. The plugin's cleanupOrphans deletes
any file in this directory carrying that marker or the generated banner;
this file survives regeneration precisely because it carries neither.
- Do NOT edit index.ts to fix imports. It is regenerated from
src/lib/mcp/index.ts on every vite dev/build, so an edit there is lost. That
is the whole reason the fix lives in an import map instead.
- Keep these versions in step with index.ts. It pins @lovable.dev/mcp-js and
zod by exact specifier, and an import-map key that does not match the
specifier in the file is silently ignored — you would be back to 25 MB with
nothing saying so. If the plugin is upgraded, update all three keys and
re-check `deno info` reports npmPackages: 0.
- No deno.lock is committed beside this file. Running deno locally against
this config writes one; do not commit it. The repo's other 366 esm.sh
imports are unpinned, and a lockfile here would fail the deploy on any
esm.sh rebuild — a new failure mode for the one function whose entire
problem was that it could not deploy. Verify with `deno info` instead.
